source_text: 从前，有个农夫正在地里耕作，突然看见一只兔子飞奔而过，撞在一棵大树上死了。农夫 毫不费力就吃到了兔肉，心里非常高兴。他想，“如果总是这样该多好啊厂'于是，他不再耕作, 每天守候在那棵树旁，等待着能再捡到撞死在树上的兔子。他等呀等，等了一天又一天，田 地也荒芜了，却再也没有等到第二只兔子。人们因而都嘲笑他把偶然当成了必然。
reference_translation: Once upon a time, there was a farmer working in the field. Suddenly, he saw a rabbit running past at full speed and hitting a big tree, then it died. The farmer ate the rabbit meat without any effort and was very happy. He thought, "How wonderful it would be if this could always happen!" So, he stopped farming and waited beside that tree every day, hoping to pick up another rabbit that had hit the tree and died. He waited and waited, day after day. The fields became deserted, but he never waited for a second rabbit. Therefore, people all laughed at him for taking the accidental as the inevitable.
